To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mechanism of the selective trapping of bacteria by the mixed bacterial imprinted films (BIF) is based on the specific binding of nanoscales surface chemical structure of bacteria to the molecular recognition sites of the BIF.

the selective binding of bacteria sensitive to nanoscale surface chemistry can be achieved by molecular imprinting technique and the mechanism of selective trapping of damaged bacteria can be explained by the dynamic Monte Carlo simulation.

the selective binding of bacteria sensitive to nanoscale surface structure to the polymer film is achieved, and the mechanism of selective trapping in an external field can be well explained from the viewpoint of electromagnetic interaction between the bacteria and the polymer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of external field-mediated selective trapping of bacteria based on their nanoscale chemical structures.
the mechanism of external field-mediated selective trapping of bacteria sensitive to nanoscale surface structure of bacteria.

the development of a new method for the rapid and highly sensitive detection of food poisoning bacteria by using a mixed bacterial imprinted polymer (BIP) and an alternating electric field, which is a new application of the molecular imprinting technique.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dielectrophoretically selective trapping of bacteria is based on the electromagnetic interaction with the nanoscale chemical structure of bacteria, and the specific binding of MRS and SCS is governed by the dynamic Monte Carlo simulation under the electromagnetic interaction.
the dielectrophoretically induced trapping of bacteria is based on the specific interaction between SCS and MRS.

the mechanism of selective trapping of bacteria in the mixed BIF can be explained by the dynamic Monte Carlo simulation, in which the dielectrophoretically enhanced trapping depends on the change in SCS, and the electromagnetic interaction is the key factor for the trapping mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dielectrophoretically induced specific trapping of bacteria is due to a change in SCS caused by the damage to the bacterial cell wall, which can be explained by the simulation of the electromagnetic interaction between the bacteria and the molecular recognition site.
the specific recognition between SCS and MRS is realized by dielectrophoretically trapping bacteria with the SCS similar to the MRS.

the specific binding of bacteria SCS to MRS in BIF is controlled by the electromagnetic interaction between the bacteria and BIF, and the specific trapping of bacteria by the dielectrophoreticity is affected by the SCS change of bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to produce a polymer film with the imprint of the nanoscale surface structure of bacteria, and the film can be used to selectively bind the original bacteria.

the specific binding of bacteria to a BIF depends on the change in their surface chemical structure (SCS), which is well explained by the dynamic Monte Carlo simulation based on the electromagnetic interaction.
the dielectrophoretically selective trapping of bacteria is strongly dependent on change in S.C.S. of bacteria damaged by heat, UV irradiation, or antibiotics.
